hasPart.description: If you have bulging eyes, you may notice they seem to stick out more than usual and you can see more of the whites of your eyes.

image.name: A close-up of a bulging eye from the side. The eye is sticking out more than usual and a lot of the white of the eyeball is showing.

hasPart.text:
You may have bulging eyes if:

  • your eyes seem to be sticking out more than usual
  • you can see less of your upper eye lids (your eyes might look like they’re open very wide)
  • you can see more of the whites of your eyes

Any other symptoms you have will depend on what's causing your eyes to stick out, but could include:

  • pain or problems closing your eyes or moving them around
  • dry eyes or feeling like there’s dirt or grit in them
  • your eyes are uncomfortable in, or sensitive to, bright light
  • blurred or double vision

hasPart.headline: Symptoms of bulging eyes

hasPart.description: A common cause of bulging eyes is a problem with the thyroid gland, but it can also be caused by other things such as an infection.

hasPart.text:
A common cause of bulging eyes is an overactive thyroid gland (hyperthyroidism).

This is where the thyroid gland (a small gland in your neck), produces too much of the thyroid hormones.

Less common causes of bulging eyes include:

  • an infection or injury around or behind your eyes
  • bleeding behind the eyes or problems with blood vessels behind the eyes
  • tumours, including those caused by neuroblastoma and some soft tissue sarcomas

hasPart.headline: Causes of bulging eyes
See a GP if:
hasPart.text: • you have a bulging eye or bulging eyes

hasPart.headline: Call 999 or go to A&E immediately if:
hasPart.text:
• your child's eye or eyes have just started bulging
  • your eye or eyes have started bulging and you have any changes to your vision, like wavy lines, flashing or loss of vision
  • your eye or eyes have started bulging and you have a severe headache or feel sick
  • you have severe eye pain, or severe eye pain that started suddenly

hasPart.headline: A&E safety messaging
hasPart.text:
Do not drive to A&E. Ask someone to drive you or call 999 and ask for an ambulance.

Bring any medicines you take with you.

hasPart.text:
Treatment for bulging eyes depends on the cause.

You may need:

  • eyedrops, gels or ointments
  • medicine prescribed by a doctor (if the bulging is caused by an infection, swelling, or a problem with your thyroid gland)
  • surgery to correct any bulging that does not go away after other treatments

If the cause is not clear, a GP may refer you to a specialist and you may need further tests.

hasPart.headline: Treatment for bulging eyes

hasPart.description: If you have bulging eyes, there are some things you can do to help the problem, such as raising your head while lying down and not smoking.

hasPart.text: If you have bulging eyes, there are things you can do to help ease your symptoms.

hasPart.headline: Do
hasPart.text:
• use pillows to keep your head raised up when lying down

  • wear sunglasses if your eyes are sensitive in bright light

  • if you wear contact lenses, take them out and wear glasses to rest your eyes

hasPart.headline: Don't
hasPart.text:
• do not smoke or drink too much alcohol

  • do not spend too long in smoky, dry or dusty places

  • do not spend too long in air conditioned or heated rooms

hasPart.headline: Things you can do if you have bulging eyes

hasPart.description: Bulging eyes (also called exophthalmos) are often caused by problems with the thyroid gland. Treatment is often needed.

hasPart.text: If you have bulging eyes, you may notice they seem to stick out more than usual and you can see more of the whites of your eyes.
A common cause of bulging eyes is a problem with the thyroid gland, but it can also be caused by other things such as an infection.
Treatment for bulging eyes depends on the cause. It might include eyedrops and medicine to treat any problems with your thyroid gland.
If you have bulging eyes, there are some things you can do to help the problem, such as raising your head while lying down and not smoking.

sections.heading: Treatment for bulging eyes
sections.text:
Treatment for bulging eyes
Treatment for bulging eyes depends on the cause.
You may need:
eyedrops, gels or ointments
medicine prescribed by a doctor (if the bulging is caused by an infection, swelling, or a problem with your thyroid gland)
surgery to correct any bulging that does not go away after other treatments
If the cause is not clear, a GP may refer you to a specialist and you may need further tests.

headings.text: Things you can do if you have bulging eyes

sections.text:
Things you can do if you have bulging eyes
If you have bulging eyes, there are things you can do to help ease your symptoms.
Do
use pillows to keep your head raised up when lying down
wear sunglasses if your eyes are sensitive in bright light
if you wear contact lenses, take them out and wear glasses to rest your eyes
Don’t
do not smoke or drink too much alcohol
do not spend too long in smoky, dry or dusty places
do not spend too long in air conditioned or heated rooms
